propositions.text: This is an application for judicial review by Mayra Aguirre Renteria challenging a decision by a Senior Immigration Officer denying her application for permanent residency on humanitarian and compassionate grounds.
propositions.quote: This is an application for judicial review by Mayra Aguirre Renteria [Ms. Aguirre] challenging a decision by a Senior Immigration Officer [the Officer] denying her application for permanent residency on humanitarian and compassionate [H & C] grounds.

paragraphs.summary: The court states that Ms. Aguirre seeks judicial review of a denial of her H&C permanent residency application by an immigration officer.

propositions.text: Ms. Aguirre is a 30-year-old black woman from Colombia who came to Canada in 2015 and claimed refugee protection, which was denied.
propositions.quote: Ms. Aguirre is a 30-year-old black woman who came to Canada in 2015 from Colombia. Later that year, she claimed refugee protection but that claim was ultimately denied.

propositions.text: Ms. Aguirre gave birth to a daughter in Vancouver on December 18, 2015.
propositions.quote: Ms. Aguirre gave birth to a daughter in Vancouver on December 18, 2015.

propositions.text: The expectation is that both Ms. Aguirre and her daughter would return to Colombia if Ms. Aguirre is removed.
propositions.quote: The expectation is that both would return to Colombia if Ms. Aguirre is removed.

paragraphs.summary: The court describes Ms. Aguirre's background, her denied refugee claim, her Canadian-born daughter, and the expectation of their return to Colombia if removed.

propositions.text: Ms. Aguirre and her brother applied for H&C relief on September 25, 2017.
propositions.quote: Ms. Aguirre and her brother, Arinson, applied for H & C relief on September 25, 2017.

propositions.text: Ms. Aguirre sought relief based on her Canadian child’s best interests, establishment, and health considerations.
propositions.quote: Ms. Aguirre sought relief based on the best interests of her Canadian child, establishment factors and health considerations.

propositions.text: Her claim was rejected on May 15, 2018, and this is the decision under challenge.
propositions.quote: Her claim was rejected on May 15, 2018. This is the decision she seeks to challenge on this application.

paragraphs.summary: The court explains Ms. Aguirre's H&C application grounds, the rejection date, and that this is the decision being challenged.

propositions.text: The application is allowed.
propositions.quote: the application is allowed.

propositions.text: The determinative issue is the sufficiency of the Officer’s best interest of a child (BIOC) analysis.
propositions.quote: The determinative issue concerns the sufficiency of the Officer’s best interest of a child [BIOC] analysis.

propositions.text: It is unnecessary to consider all other arguments beyond noting the Officer’s treatment of Ms. Aguirre’s medical situation was also lacking.
propositions.quote: It is unnecessary for me to consider all of the other arguments presented by counsel beyond the observation that the Officer’s treatment of Ms. Aguirre’s medical situation also left something to be desired.

paragraphs.summary: The court allows the application, finding the BIOC analysis determinative, and notes the Officer's handling of medical issues was also lacking.

propositions.text: Ms. Aguirre’s challenge to the Officer’s BIOC analysis raises an issue of mixed fact and law, reviewed for reasonableness.
propositions.quote: Ms. Aguirre’s challenge to the Officer’s BIOC analysis raises an issue of mixed fact and law and stands to be reviewed on the standard of reasonableness

propositions.text: Significant deference is owed to H&C decision-makers, but deference does not constitute a 'blank cheque'.
propositions.quote: while significant deference is owed to H & C decision-makers, deference does not constitute a “blank cheque”.

propositions.text: Reasons must meet requirements of transparency, justification, and intelligibility as described in Dunsmuir v New Brunswick.
propositions.quote: The reasons given must still meet the requirements of transparency, justification and intelligibility as described in Dunsmuir v New Brunswick

paragraphs.summary: The court states the standard of review is reasonableness, referencing Kanthasamy and Miyir, and emphasizes the need for transparent, justified, and intelligible reasons.

propositions.text: The Officer’s BIOC comments lack meaningful analysis of hardships faced by a black child in Colombia.
propositions.quote: The Officer’s BIOC comments contain no meaningful analysis of the evidence concerning the hardships faced by a black child living in Colombia.

propositions.text: The decision only contains unhelpful truisms and a tepid acknowledgement of less favourable conditions for Afro-Colombians.
propositions.quote: the description of the prevailing conditions is limited to the tepid acknowledgement that “current country conditions for Afro-Colombians are less than favourable”.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the Officer's BIOC analysis lacks meaningful engagement with evidence of hardships for black children in Colombia, offering only superficial observations.

propositions.text: A proper BIOC analysis requires more than superficial reference to evidence.
propositions.quote: To carry out a proper BIOC analysis it is not enough to pay half-hearted lip-service to the evidence.

propositions.text: The Minister argues sufficiency of reasons can be disregarded because relevant evidence was obviously considered and weighed in favour of the family.
propositions.quote: I reject the Minister’s argument that the sufficiency of reasons concern can reasonably be disregarded on judicial review because the relevant evidence was obviously considered and weighed in favour of the family.

propositions.text: The court rejects the Minister’s argument about sufficiency of reasons.
propositions.quote: I reject the Minister’s argument that the sufficiency of reasons concern can reasonably be disregarded on judicial review because the relevant evidence was obviously considered and weighed in favour of the family.

paragraphs.summary: The court states a proper BIOC analysis requires substantive engagement with evidence and rejects the Minister's argument that sufficiency of reasons can be disregarded.

propositions.text: Kanthasamy requires BIOC analysis to consider many factors about a child's welfare, including country conditions, education, special needs, health care, and gender.
propositions.quote: the BIOC analysis required of an H & C review requires consideration of a multitude of factors relating to a child’s emotional, social, cultural and physical welfare. Included on the list are country conditions, education, special needs, health care and matters related to gender.

propositions.text: Children are often deserving of special consideration and their interests must be given significant weight in H&C analysis.
propositions.quote: We are also told that children are often deserving of special consideration and that their interests are to be given significant weight in the overall H & C analysis.

propositions.text: It is not enough to state that a child's best interests have been considered; there must be meaningful engagement with the evidence.
propositions.quote: It is not enough to state that the best interests of a child affected by a removal from Canada have been taken into account.

propositions.text: H&C decision-makers must substantively consider and weigh all relevant facts and factors before them.
propositions.quote: H & C decision-makers “must substantively consider and weigh all the relevant facts and factors before them”.

paragraphs.summary: The court summarizes Kanthasamy's requirements for BIOC analysis, emphasizing meaningful engagement with evidence and significant weight to children's interests.

propositions.text: The Officer’s bare acknowledgement of less favourable conditions in Colombia was insufficient.
propositions.quote: In this case, the bare acknowledgement by the Officer of less favourable conditions in Colombia was insufficient.

propositions.text: Ms. Aguirre was entitled to know why those conditions were not considered deserving of relief when weighed in the evidentiary balance.
propositions.quote: What Ms. Aguirre was entitled to know is why those less favourable conditions were considered to be undeserving of relief when weighed in the evidentiary balance.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the Officer's minimal acknowledgment of Colombian conditions inadequate and states Ms. Aguirre deserved an explanation for the denial of relief.

propositions.text: The record before the Officer included significant evidence that women, blacks, and children in Colombia face significant hardships in almost all aspects of life.
propositions.quote: The record before the Officer contained a significant body of country condition evidence indicating that women, blacks and children in Colombia face significant hardships in almost all aspects of life.

propositions.text: Afro-Colombians face a long-standing, pervasive history of racial inequality and prejudice.
propositions.quote: At the root of much of the difficulty faced by Afro-Colombians is a long-standing, pervasive history of racial inequality and prejudice.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes the record showed significant hardships for women, blacks, and children in Colombia, rooted in racial inequality and prejudice.

propositions.text: Black women and children are particularly at risk, with discrimination often manifested in violence.
propositions.quote: Black women and children are particularly at risk. Discrimination against Afro-Colombians is often manifested in violence

paragraphs.summary: The court states black women and children in Colombia are especially at risk, facing violence due to discrimination.

propositions.text: A 2017 UN report highlights pervasive structural discrimination against Afro-Colombians, including in education, employment, housing, political participation, and justice.
propositions.quote: Afro-Colombian representatives highlight pervasive structural discrimination, including access to quality education, employment and participation in economic life, housing, effective political participation and access to justice.

propositions.text: The illiteracy index among Afro-Colombians is 30%, compared to the national average of 16%.
propositions.quote: The estimated illiteracy index within the Afro-Colombian population is 30 per cent, compared with the national average of 16 per cent.

propositions.text: Nearly 10% of Afro-Colombian children aged 6-10 do not access primary education, with higher rates in some regions.
propositions.quote: Nearly 10 per cent of Afro-Colombian children from 6 to 10 years of age do not access primary education, with the percentage believed to be far higher in some regions.

paragraphs.summary: A 2017 UN report documents pervasive discrimination against Afro-Colombians, high illiteracy, and poor access to education for children.

propositions.text: The record disclosed that Afro-Colombian women are often targets of sexual violence and exploitation.
propositions.quote: The record also disclosed that Afro-Colombian women are often the targets of sexual violence and exploitation

propositions.text: Sexual exploitation of children was also a reported problem.
propositions.quote: Sexual exploitation of children was also a reported problem

paragraphs.summary: The court notes evidence that Afro-Colombian women and children face sexual violence and exploitation in Colombia.

propositions.text: A non-governmental organization reported the quality of educational opportunities for black students in Colombia is poor or very poor.
propositions.quote: The quality of educational opportunities for black students was said by one non-governmental organization to be poor or very poor

paragraphs.summary: A non-governmental organization reported poor educational opportunities for black students in Colombia.

propositions.text: Another report states unemployment disproportionately affects women, who also face discrimination in hiring and wages.
propositions.quote: According to another report, unemployment disproportionally affects women who also face discrimination in hiring and wages

propositions.text: The US Department of State Report for 2016 described child abuse and sexual exploitation of children as serious problems.
propositions.quote: The United States Department of State Report for 2016 described child abuse as a serious problem along with sexual exploitation of children

propositions.text: Afro-Colombians face significant economic and social discrimination despite constitutional rights and protections.
propositions.quote: Afro-Colombians are entitled to all constitutional rights and protections, but they faced significant economic and social discrimination.

propositions.text: In Choco, with the highest percentage of Afro-Colombians, 79% lived below the poverty line and 32% in extreme poverty.
propositions.quote: in Choco, the department with the highest percentage of Afro-Colombian residents, 79 percent of residents lived below the poverty line. NGO Afro- Colombian Solidarity Network reported 32 percent of Choco’s residents lived in extreme poverty.

propositions.text: Choco had the lowest per capita social investment, ranked last in infrastructure, education, and health, and had the highest income inequality in Colombia.
propositions.quote: Choco continued to experience the lowest per capita level of social investment; ranked last among departments in terms of infrastructure, education, and health; and experienced the highest rate of income inequality in the country.

paragraphs.summary: Reports show women face employment discrimination, child abuse and exploitation are serious problems, and Afro-Colombians, especially in Choco, face severe poverty and inequality.

propositions.text: A 2013 human rights report stated Afro-Colombians face high informal labour, unemployment, dropout rates, illiteracy, poor water and sanitation, child labour, and limited government services.
propositions.quote: A 2013 human rights report stated that Afro-Colombians are plagued by high rates of informal labour, unemployment, high drop-out rates, illiteracy, poor access to potable water and sanitation, child labour and limited access to government services

paragraphs.summary: A 2013 human rights report details multiple hardships faced by Afro-Colombians, including unemployment, illiteracy, and poor access to services.

propositions.text: The Officer failed to ask or answer whether returning Ms. Aguirre and her child to Colombia would be unacceptable to fair-minded Canadians.
propositions.quote: The question the Officer failed to ask or answer is whether the return of Ms. Aguirre and her Canadian infant to the general conditions described above (and elsewhere in the record) would be considered by decent fair-minded Canadians to be unacceptable.

propositions.text: The court’s role is not to answer that question but to ensure it receives reasonable consideration and articulation.
propositions.quote: It is not my role to answer that question but only to ensure that it receives reasonable consideration and articulation.

propositions.text: In this case, the question did not receive reasonable consideration or articulation.
propositions.quote: In this case, it did not.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the Officer failed to reasonably consider or articulate whether returning Ms. Aguirre and her child to Colombia would be unacceptable.

propositions.text: The decision is set aside and the matter is to be redetermined on the merits by a different decision-maker.
propositions.quote: the decision is set aside. The matter is to be redetermined on the merits by a different decision-maker.

propositions.text: The Applicant may update the evidentiary record due to the passage of time.
propositions.quote: Given the passage of time, the Applicant will be entitled to update the evidentiary record.

paragraphs.summary: The court sets aside the decision, orders redetermination by a different decision-maker, and allows the Applicant to update the evidence.

propositions.text: Neither party proposed a certified question and no issue of general importance arises on this record.
propositions.quote: Neither party proposed a certified question and no issue of general importance arises on this record.

propositions.text: The application is allowed and the matter is to be redetermined by a different decision-maker.
propositions.quote: THIS COURT’S JUDGMENT is that this application is allowed with the matter to be redetermined on the merits by a different decision-maker.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes no certified question was proposed, finds no issue of general importance, and formally allows the application for redetermination.
